original_question: Let Z(s) = product_{n>=1} (1 - lambda_n(s)^2) be the Selberg zeta function written in terms of the canonically indexed eigenvalues lambda_n(s) of the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator. For k in N, the order of vanishing of Z(s) at s = 1 - k equals dim_C(M_{2k}), where M_{2k} is the corresponding space of cusp forms for PSL_2(Z). Determine how the quantity dim_C(M_{2k}) is distributed among the individual factors in the product Z(1 - k) = product_{n>=1} (1 - lambda_n(1 - k)^2).
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 5: the problem about the trivial zeros of the Selberg zeta function Z(s) and how the quantity dim_C(M_{2k}) is distributed among the canonically indexed factors in the product Z(1-k)=product_{n>=1}(1-lambda_n(1-k)^2). The notation comes from the immediately preceding setup in Section 3 defining L_s, Z(s), and the canonical indexing of lambda_n(s). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
correct_elements: Your draft is already aimed at the right place in the paper and gets the core mathematical objects right: the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator, the factorization Z(s)=product_{n>=1}(1-lambda_n(s)^2), the special points s=1-k with k in N, and the question of how the multiplicity dim_C(M_{2k}) should be apportioned among the individual factors. It also preserves the paper's emphasis that the indexing of the eigenvalues is canonical. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
missing_details: The paper first fixes the ambient analytic setup: D={z in C: |z-1|<3/2} and V is the Banach space of functions analytic on D and continuous on its closure, with the supremum norm. Your draft omits this operator-theoretic context. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The operator itself should be stated exactly as L_s[f](z)=sum_{m>=1}(z+m)^(-2s) f(1/(z+m)) for Re(s)>1/2, together with the note that L_s is analytically continued to all complex s. Your draft mentions the operator only informally. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The paper ties the product to the Selberg zeta function by the determinant identity det(1-L_s^2)=product_{n>=1}(1-lambda_n(s)^2)=Z(s) for the full modular group PSL_2(Z). This exact identity and the group PSL_2(Z) should be included to make the question stand-alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The canonical indexing is not just any enumeration: the paper says that the labeling by n is canonical, corresponds to polynomials of degree n+1, and agrees with ordering the eigenvalues by magnitude. Your draft mentions canonical indexing but not the paper's precise nearby description of it. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
The paper fixes k in N explicitly. That quantifier should appear at the start of the question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The phrase 'distributed among the individual factors' needs sharpening: because Z(1-k) itself is zero when the multiplicity is positive, the mathematically faithful stand-alone version should ask which factors 1-lambda_n(s)^2 contribute to the zero at s=1-k and what contribution each makes to the total order of vanishing. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

To stay paper-faithful, the notation M_{2k} should be kept exactly as the paper states it, namely as the 'corresponding space of cusp forms M_{2k} for PSL_2(Z)'; the paper does not replace this by any broader or different notation in Problem 5 itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
refined_question: For a fixed integer k in N, let D={z in C: |z-1|<3/2}, let V be the Banach space of functions analytic on D and continuous on its closure with the supremum norm, and for Re(s)>1/2 define the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator by L_s[f](z)=sum_{m>=1}(z+m)^(-2s) f(1/(z+m)), extended analytically to all s in C. Let lambda_n(s), n>=1, be its canonically indexed eigenvalues, so that det(1-L_s^2)=product_{n>=1}(1-lambda_n(s)^2)=Z(s), where Z(s) is the Selberg zeta function for PSL_2(Z). The paper states that ord_{s=1-k} Z(s)=dim_C(M_{2k}), where M_{2k} is the corresponding space of cusp forms for PSL_2(Z). Determine how this total vanishing multiplicity dim_C(M_{2k}) is distributed among the canonically indexed factors 1-lambda_n(s)^2 at s=1-k; in other words, identify which indices n contribute to the zero at s=1-k and how much each contributing factor accounts for in the total order of vanishing. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
justification: The draft is close to the paper's actual target, but it is not yet fully stand-alone. Problem 5 is stated only after the paper introduces the Banach space V, the transfer operator L_s, the determinant identity relating its canonically indexed eigenvalues to the Selberg zeta function, and the significance of the canonical indexing. The main refinement needed is to turn the informal phrase 'distributed among the individual factors in the product Z(1-k)' into the precise question about how the order of vanishing at s=1-k decomposes factor-by-factor among 1-lambda_n(s)^2. I did not broaden the problem beyond Section 3, Problem 5, and I did not replace it with the neighboring Problem 4 about the map from Riemann zeros to eigenvalue indices. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
